checks.title: Paths from somebody's machine
checks.fix: Replace each path with one relative to the repository, an environment variable, or a setting the person provides. Then check the commit history for the same path if the name in it should not be public.

checks.title: Names on the deny list
checks.fix: Replace each name in the files listed, and reword the commit messages listed (git rebase -i, then reword) before the history is published. A name in a commit message that is already public stays public.

checks.title: A README that says how to start
A contributing guide
checks.fix: Add a CONTRIBUTING.md at the root, in .github/ or in docs/: how to set up, how to run the tests, and what a good issue and pull request look like.

checks.title: A code of conduct
checks.fix: Add a CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md at the root, in .github/ or in docs/. The Contributor Covenant is a common start; say in it who to contact about a problem.

checks.title: A security policy
checks.fix: Add a SECURITY.md at the root, in .github/ or in docs/: which versions get fixes, and how to report a vulnerability privately (GitHub's private vulnerability reporting, or an address).

checks.title: Issue and pull request templates
checks.fix: Add .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ with a bug report and a feature request, and a .github/pull_request_template.md that asks what changed, why, and how it was tested.

checks.title: Continuous integration
checks.fix: Add a workflow in .github/workflows/ that runs on push and pull_request, checks out the code, installs, and runs the build.

checks.title: Tests in CI
checks.fix: Add a step to the CI workflow that runs the project's tests (npm test, pytest, or whatever runs them here), so a pull request that breaks them shows red.

checks.title: Workflow token permissions
checks.fix: Add `permissions: contents: read` at the top of each workflow listed, and grant more only in the job that needs it.

checks.title: pull_request_target with the pull request's code
checks.fix: Use pull_request instead, which runs a fork's code without this repository's secrets. If the workflow must use pull_request_target, never check out or run the pull request's head in it.

checks.title: Untrusted input in a workflow's shell
checks.fix: Move each expression into an env: entry on the step and use the variable in the shell, quoted ("$TITLE"), so the text is data and never code.

checks.title: A lockfile
checks.fix: Run npm install (or your package manager's install) beside each package.json listed and commit the lockfile it writes.

checks.title: Known advisories in dependencies
checks.reason: This reads the npm lockfile, and there isn't one: deps.lockfile has the fix.

checks.title: Automated dependency updates
checks.fix: Add a .github/dependabot.yml for each ecosystem in the repository (or a Renovate configuration), so updates arrive as pull requests.
